newsitem.title: CHINA: China newspapers warn on stock market overheating.
newsitem.headline: China newspapers warn on stock market overheating.

text.p: China's official financial newspapers on Monday warned that the country's stock markets are again becoming overheated and said investors should take care to avoid falling into a trap set by manipulators.
"In only three months, the Shanghai stock market has risen nearly 40 percent and the Shenzhen market more than 40 percent," an editorial by the China Securities newspaper said.
"Compared with China's overall economic development, the markets have displayed signs of overheating."
"With prices of shares doubling and doubling again, it is possible that some manipulators are setting a trap for you to fall into," an editorial in the Shanghai Securities News said.
"Who can guarantee that the huge funds flowing onto the primary (share issue) market all come from legitimate sources?" it added.

The sternly-worded editorials were reminiscent of a commentary published last December by the People's Daily, mouthpiece of the Communist Party, which said the government would not rescue investors if stock prices collapsed.
The commentary, aimed at cooling over-speculation, pushed share prices down by more than 30 percent, but the markets have since recovered all the lost ground.
